findings.rule: Density tiers (deep dive: ONE focal element, usually the anatomy diagram or the segment table)
findings.evidence: The veins table is the focal element, but at 1440 it is clipped at the right inner edge of its deck (x≈875). The 7th column header reads 'PV (სმ' and every PV input is cut in half, in all three groups (IVC, right, left). The bigger diagram rail left the table column narrower than the grid's 866px min-width plus padding, so PV is only reachable by scrolling each group sideways. The patency value 'გამავალი' also shows as 'გამავალ…' beside its ×. The overlap is fixed, but the value is still cut off. DESIGN-DIRECTION.md has no rule against truncated values. I grade this as the focal table failing to show all its columns at the main desktop width.
findings.recommendation: Fit all 7 grid tracks inside the table column at 1440 with no inner horizontal scroll. Either cap the diagram rail about 40px narrower, or trim the grid gap from 10px to 8px and the segment-column minimum from 96px to about 84px. Re-check at 1440 that the 'PV (სმ/წმ)' header and inputs show in full and the patency select shows 'გამავალი' untruncated.

findings.rule: Density tiers (one focal element that wins on weight)
findings.evidence: At a 1440×900 viewport, three things fill y=0–600: the banner, a separate row holding only 'შაბლონები' and '+ ახალი შემთხვევა', and the clinical-context deck (about 380px, five mostly empty inputs). The first table data row starts around y=900 and the diagram image around y=840. So on load the eye lands on empty context inputs rather than the table or diagram. Ordering and depth are correct (decks lift off the page at a 1.2 contrast ratio), but the focal pair does not win the first view.
findings.recommendation: Move 'შაბლონები' and 'ახალი შემთხვევა' into the banner's right-hand action group, next to 'კვლევის დამატება', so their separate row goes away. Lay out the clinical-context deck in two rows: სქესი + სიმპტომები + თანმხლები on the first, მიდგომები + პოზიციები + the Valsalva checkbox on the second. That brings the table header and diagram toolbar above the fold. This moves content, so it is a layout change rather than a token swap.

findings.evidence: densityFit went 2 → 1 → 2 across rounds 1–3. The round-2 dip came only from the mechanical empty-state-parity cap on the SVP row. This round collapsed that row: SVP is now a one-line row with no subtitle, visibly quieter than the CEAP row, and the metrics no longer report the failure (classification ratio 0.64). The cause is a real defect that has been fixed, not two rules in conflict.
findings.recommendation: No product decision needed. Confirm densityFit holds at 2 on the next run. If it drops again without a new mechanical failure, escalate.

reasoning: The light capture matches the light metrics (colorScheme light, no hard fails, elevation 1.2, 5/8 decks shadowed). It was judged against deep-dive.png. findings.rule: Empty states collapse (equal-size cards make a normal study look identical to a heavily abnormal one) + Density tiers
findings.evidence: IliacCavalTable.tsx opens every populated row by default (`const open = openOverride[id] ?? populated`). So one tap on 'ყველა ნორმაში' expands all 21 segment cards, each about 240px tall with 6 fields. The page grows to 8062px. An all-normal study is now the longest page this screen can produce, and it looks exactly like a fully abnormal one. The diagram and conclusion are pushed about 6,500px down. In round 2 the same rows were one-line collapsed rows.
findings.recommendation: On compact widths, open a row by default only when it holds an abnormal or measured value: patency other than გამავალი, a reflux value, competency other than კომპეტენტური, or an AP/PV number. Rows that are normal stay collapsed as one line, with a muted --emr-text-secondary summary such as 'გამავალი · სრული · კომპეტენტური' in place of the badge. This changes behaviour, not tokens.

findings.evidence: redundancy has gone 1 → 3 → 1 across rounds 1–3. Nine of the twelve duplicate-primary-data hits are bilateral segment names ('CIV პროქს.' right vs left) and the '· მარჯვენა/· მარცხენა' suffix that round 2 required so each bilateral segment reads as distinct. Two rules now conflict: 'side must make each bilateral segment distinct' and the duplicate detector, which treats the same segment name on two sides as duplicate data.
findings.recommendation: Escalate to the founder as a product or tooling decision. Either (a) accept that bilateral segment titles are distinct data and exempt `iliac-caval-toggle-*-right/-left` row titles from duplicate-primary-data, or (b) remove the per-row side suffix and rely on the 'მარჯვენა/მარცხენა' group header, accepting that the round-2 disambiguation finding comes back on mobile. Stop iterating on this dimension until that is chosen.

reasoning: The light capture matches the light metrics. It was judged against deep-dive.png and inferred as a 768 single-column stack. The metrics report a white page background (contrast 1.0), but the screenshot clearly shows a gray page under white, shadowed decks, and no elevation hard fail was emitted, so I treat it as a scope quirk. The real problem comes from the data state. This capture used 'ყველა ნორმაში', and because populated rows open themselves, every segment becomes a full expanded card with the same blue 'შევსებულია' chip. A clinician scrolls through 21 identical normal cards to reach the diagram and conclusion, and a normal study looks like a busy abnormal one. Colour is still disciplined: no severity colour appears outside its role, and there is one gradient primary. Nothing in the cards is loud. They are uniform and quiet, so restraint holds at 2. The repetition is a footprint problem, scored under densityFit 1. The mechanical cap puts redundancy at 1. Most of those hits are legitimate bilateral names, which I escalate as an oscillation. Highest-leverage fix: open only rows with abnormal or measured values, and collapse normal rows to a muted one-line summary with no badge. That one change shrinks the page by about 4,000px and removes the 21-chip repetition.

The 'შევსებულია' chip squeezes the row title, so right and left titles truncate exactly where the side is written: 'CIV შუა · მარჯვ…', 'CIV დისტ. · მარ…', 'EIV პროქს. · მა…'. The side suffix, the one part added to tell bilateral rows apart, is the part that gets cut off.

findings.evidence: redundancy has gone 1 → 3 → 1 across rounds 1–3. The hits are mostly bilateral segment names and the side suffix that round 2 required. 'Side must make each bilateral segment distinct' conflicts with the duplicate detector's same-text rule.

reasoning: The light capture matches the light metrics. It was judged against deep-dive.png as a 375 single-column stack. The failure comes from the data state. 'ყველა ნორმაში' opens all 21 segment cards, each about 540px, so a normal study becomes an 18-screen scroll of identical cards with identical blue chips. findings.rule: Color discipline (dark mode via semantic vars only; never non-token surfaces) + reference parity (surface treatment)
findings.evidence: The pelvic illustration is a raster image on a pure-white background. In dark mode it shows as a white block of about 470×380px at y≈900–1390 inside a rgb(30,41,59) deck. It is by far the brightest thing on the page, brighter than any text or the primary button, and this round's enlargement doubled its area. deep-dive-dark.png has no light surface anywhere. The diagram should be the focal element, but here it wins by glare, not design.
findings.recommendation: Ship the pelvic illustration with a transparent background, as a PNG or SVG, so it sits on --emr-bg-card like the other studies' anatomy views. Until then, give the image a 12px-radius inset frame with an --emr-border-color hairline, so it reads as a deliberate film panel rather than a hole in the deck. This ties into the open founder decision: if the diagram becomes a colouring-book SVG, it picks up the dark tokens automatically.
